To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the topological susceptibility of the center vortex model is compatible with lattice measurements, and that the model can thus be used to describe the infrared sector of SU(2), but not of SU(3), Yang–Mills theories.
the topological susceptibility of Yang–Mills theories can be computed within the center vortex model, and that the result of this computation is in agreement with the lattice data.

a definition of the Pontraygin index for center vortex world-surfa ces composed of plaquetes on a hypercubical lattice is constructed, and that it is used to evaluate in a model the topological susceptibility of Yang-Mills theory, which turns out to be compatible with lattice measurements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the topological structure of SU(2)-Yang-Mills theory in the infrared regime.
the topological susceptibility of Yang–Mills (YM) theory in the infrared sector of the theory.
the study of a random surface model for center vortices in the infrared sector of SU(2)-Yang–Mills theory, which has been shown to be able to account for the confinement of static quarks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the center vortex model is a good description of the confinement sector of SU(2)-Yang-Mills theory.
the center vortex model is a viable model for the infrared behavior of Yang–Mills gauge theories.
the center vortex model provides a very plausible and attractive picture for the infrared sector in SU(2) pure Yang–Mills gauge theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the center vortex model for SU(2), which is based on the assumption that the infrared sector of SU(2)-YangMills theory is dominated by center vortices, is able to describe the confinement properties of this theory and also the topological structure of the vacuum.
the random surface model for the center vortices is able to describe the infrared sector of pure Yang–Mills dynamics.

the center vortex model is able to reproduce all relevant infrared properties of SU( 2) Yang– Mills theory, i.e. the string tension, the deconfinement transition, the topological susceptibility, and the magnetic mass.
The main takeaway from our work is that
center vortices can account for all the non-perturbative properties of Yang–Mills theories.
the center vortex model for confinement can be extended to include a topological sector which is consistent with the topological properties of Yang–Mills theories.
the center vortex model is a promising candidate for a description of the low-energy sector of SU(2)-Yang–Mills theory in four space-time dimensions.
